text:
Marco: Hey all — quick follow-up from today's all-hands people-ops segment. Two quick things: 1) Can you clarify the promotion queue timeline (when managers need to submit packet vs when decisions are communicated)? 2) Any update on how comp bands will be applied for internal moves? :thinking:

People Ops: Great questions — thanks for flagging, Marco. Short answers here then we can expand. 1) Promotion packet deadline is manager-submitted by Mar 5. Calibration window is Mar 8–Mar 15. Final decisions communicated Mar 20. 2) For internal moves we use the same comp bands but with targeted market adjustment where warranted — more below. :wave:

Marco: Awesome — is there a public doc with the exact checklist managers should follow?

People Ops: Yes — we just updated the Promos & Reviews doc (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/promotions). Top of the doc has a checklist. Copying the key bits here: 

```
Manager checklist (high level):
- Fill promo rationale + evidence (examples of impact)
- Peer/skip-level feedback attached
- Updated role profile + new responsibilities
- Manager calibration notes
- Compensation recommendation (range + target comp)
```

People Ops: For the timeline, here's the quick view we shared in the all-hands: 

```
- Feb 20: Managers kickoff
- Mar 5: Packet deadline (manager submit)
- Mar 8-15: Calibration panels
- Mar 20: Decisions shared to managers
- Mar 25: HR publishes offer letters/comp changes
```

Anya: Thanks — quick follow-up: if a manager misses the Mar 5 deadline because of team bandwidth, is there a late process?

People Ops: We try to avoid exceptions to keep calibration fair. If a manager misses it we ask them to escalate to their ELT lead and we allow a short grace window to Mar 9, but that metadata (late submission) is recorded and may affect prioritization. Please coordinate with your People Partner if you foresee delays.

Jamal: On comp bands: will mid-cycle internal promotions get pro-rated increases or full band moves?

People Ops: Typically internal promotions that change level get an immediate band move; comp increase size is based on role/level and tenure. Small promotions (within same band) may be title-only. If comp budget is a constraint, we apply a phased increase (e.g., partial now, remainder after next cycle) — that happens ~10% of cases.

Sarah: Is there a clear formula for merit increases vs promotion increases? Some managers ask for guidance when writing packets.

People Ops: Short version: merit increases (annual review) are budget-driven and roughly based on performance percentiles. Promotion increases are role/level adjustments tied to market and internal equity. We included an example table in the promo doc with typical ranges: 

- Merit: 0-8% (typical performers 3-5%)
- Promotion to next level: 8-20% (depends on market gap and level)

Rafael: Will these numbers be visible to managers in the compensation tool, or is it just a guideline?

People Ops: Managers will see target ranges + suggested offer in the compensation tool — final offer still requires HR approval for equity/leveling checks.

Eva: Any updates on benefits changes that were hinted at in the all-hands? Was PTO policy being adjusted?

People Ops: We're piloting a flexible PTO accrual policy for small teams (engineering + product pilot) starting Apr 1. No change to base accrual yet for company-wide. We will publish pilot details next week and invite volunteers.

Marco: Thanks — super helpful. One last ask: can People Ops host an open office hour for managers to go through packet examples?

People Ops: Yes — we'll host two sessions next week: Tue 10am PT and Thu 4pm PT. Sign-up link: https://redwood.internal/events/promo-office-hours. We'll drop sample packets and a checklist in the calendar invite. :calendar:

HR-bot: Reminder scheduled: Promo packet deadline in 12 days (Mar 5) — please upload to the promotions folder.

Anya: Sweet. I'll forward to my managers. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

People Ops: Thanks — keep the questions coming here and we'll update the promo doc with any clarifications.

Jamal: One last tiny question — are L5 -> L6 promotions automatically reviewed by the executive review panel or only when comp gap > 15%?

People Ops: L5->L6 goes to exec review when comp impact exceeds our threshold OR the role is cross-functional. If it's a standard IC growth move with minimal comp delta, it stays in manager + calibration panel. We'll add that rule to the doc.

Sarah: Appreciate the quick clarifications. :heart:

People Ops: Closing loop — doc updated 1hr after thread start. Link again: https://redwood.internal/docs/promotions (v2).
